Building a house on Kentucky would cost $150 and raise rent to $250. That is not enough to bankrupt the opponent, so I am skipping it. The opponent's brown hotels are the bigger threat.

Extracting cash from the opponent would shrink their survival margin and make Park Place lethal too. Liquidation equals cash plus buildings plus mortgage properties.

I also weighed offering my mortgaged railroads for a small cash sum, and noted that Ventnor Avenue could help the opponent complete the yellow group if they buy Atlantic Avenue.

I will preserve cash to survive the Baltic hotel rent of $450; my current cash of $535 leaves only an $85 margin.
